summary: The approved project-owned FHIR R4 compatibility boundary accepts the immutable synthetic seed on minimal source, JSON, required-field, reference, and content-isolation rules while preserving CARIN 2.2.0 nonconformance and opaque terminology as non-authoritative diagnostics.
decisions: DATA-001 defines a project-owned FHIR R4 compatibility profile rather than requiring base FHIR or CARIN conformance. Project acceptance is determined only by source/classification, strict JSON, supported envelope/resource/profile markers, required anchor fields, cross-file references, and content-isolation rules.

The repository-root dataset is the approved synthetic local-development source under PROJECT, SYSTEM, and ADR-0002. Its four files remain byte-identical, read-only, hash-pinned, untrusted inputs. Acquisition/license/benchmark limitations remain recorded but do not override the approved local synthetic classification.

The validation unit is the declared source set: one standalone Patient, one homogeneous Coverage searchset, one homogeneous pharmacy ExplanationOfBenefit searchset, and the provenance readme. Required Patient/Coverage references resolve across files against unique resourceType/id identities.

The minimal Patient anchors are resourceType, id, supported profile marker, non-empty identifier, and non-empty name. Coverage anchors are id, supported marker, status, type, and beneficiary.reference. EOB anchors are id, supported pharmacy marker, status, type, use, patient.reference, non-empty insurance coverage references, and non-empty item.

Supported profile markers are routing data only: each resource may carry its exact observed unversioned CARIN canonical or that canonical qualified with |2.2.0. Acceptance of the marker makes no profile-conformance claim.

Coverage and EOB envelopes are homogeneous Bundle[type=searchset] inputs. Bundle.entry.fullUrl is optional in the compatibility profile, Bundle.total may exceed page size, and paging/link/search metadata is inert preserve-only data. Other Bundle types, mixed/empty bundles, and request/response content are rejected.

Every accepted path, non-modifier extension URL, and coding system URI must be exactly enumerated in boundary.json from the immutable seed; wildcard/prefix acceptance is prohibited. New paths/systems/extensions are rejected until a reviewed contract version adds them.

Observed extensions, codes, displays, identifiers, profile markers, URLs, and non-required references are preserved as opaque untrusted data. Modifier extensions, contained resources, narratives, attachments/base64, undeclared active content, and executable Bundle surfaces are rejected.

Required Coverage-to-Patient, EOB-to-Patient, and EOB-to-Coverage references must be relative, same-source-set, expected-type, and uniquely resolvable. Other references are preserve-opaque and are never dereferenced or treated as authoritative evidence.

Machine results separate decision from diagnostics. Accepted results start with minimal-profile-valid, contain exactly one of carin-no-errors-reported, carin-nonconformant, or carin-diagnostic-unavailable, and may add terminology-unverified. Rejected results have decision=rejected and states=[rejected] exactly; rejected is exclusive and CARIN is not run.

The unchanged seed's expected result is decision=accepted with states ordered as minimal-profile-valid, carin-nonconformant, terminology-unverified. CARIN errors and unverified terminology remain fully visible without changing minimal acceptance.

CARIN 2.2.0, its checksum-pinned closure, publisher QA, and Validator CLI 6.10.2 remain offline diagnostic evidence only. Raw OperationOutcome evidence is retained by digest with original severity/counts and normalized sanitized findings; no CARIN result can accept or reject project input.

CARIN diagnostic unavailability does not change an input decision but produces carin-diagnostic-unavailable and fails DATA-001 verification until tooling/digests are restored. A no-error diagnostic is worded carin-no-errors-reported and never presented as a conformance claim.

NCPDP, CMS, CARIN, HL7, NDC, and other values without approved offline membership/meaning evidence produce terminology-unverified and remain opaque. No live lookup, substitute terminology, guessed membership, display inference, publisher-QA severity override, or domain-semantic claim is permitted.

Structured findings use stable project rule IDs, source/layer, original diagnostic severity where applicable, sanitized codes/messages, source paths, and JSON pointers. Raw untrusted diagnostic content is separately referenced by digest rather than interpolated into logs or instructions.

DATA-001 contract artifacts remain boundary.json, packages.lock.json, validation-outcome.schema.json, source-manifest.json, data-card.json, and README.md under contracts/fhir/data-001, with independent fixtures/harness under tests. OpenAPI, application services, persistence, UI, infrastructure, and deployment remain out of scope.

Only contract and independent testing work is required. Database, backend, frontend, and infrastructure impacts are false; PLATFORM-001 owns later runtime/API/storage/quarantine/authorization decisions without weakening the compatibility/diagnostic separation.

The prior strict-CARIN and authoritative-external-positive blockers are resolved by the approved project compatibility decision. The orchestrator must reconcile stale strict-CARIN/negative-seed acceptance text in task.json before lifecycle advancement; architect scope prohibits that edit.

risks.description: A minimal-profile-valid result could be misrepresented as base FHIR/CARIN conformance or as evidence of coverage, payment, coding, fraud, clinical, policy, or real-world correctness.
risks.mitigation: Use the exact compatibility state names, preserve CARIN diagnostics separately, prohibit conformance/domain wording, and require human/governance authority for all substantive conclusions.

risks.description: Making CARIN diagnostics advisory could lead an implementation to hide, discard, or stop running them.
risks.mitigation: Pin tool/package digests, retain raw evidence by digest plus original counts/severities, require a CARIN state on every accepted result, and fail verification when diagnostics are unavailable.

risks.description: Opaque CMS/NCPDP/CARIN codes or extension values could be treated as verified membership or payer semantics downstream.
risks.mitigation: Emit terminology-unverified with exact pointers/systems, preserve values without interpretation, prohibit inferred displays/membership, and require later approved domain/terminology contracts before semantic use.

risks.description: A broad optional-path or extension rule could silently expand the compatibility surface and admit active or meaning-changing content.
risks.mitigation: Use exact reviewed path/extension/system registries, reject unknown content, prohibit wildcards, and require versioned architecture/contract review for additions.

risks.description: Narratives, validator messages, identifiers, URLs, extensions, and display text can carry injection, active content, sensitive-looking values, or exfiltration targets.
risks.mitigation: Reject active surfaces, never render/execute/dereference source content, sanitize normalized findings, and retain lossless raw diagnostics only as separately identified untrusted artifacts.

risks.description: Cross-file references and paged Bundles can be mishandled by file-local validation or by assuming Bundle.total equals entry count.
risks.mitigation: Validate the complete declared source set, enforce unique type/id resolution, allow total greater than page size, and independently test broken, ambiguous, cross-type, and remote references.

risks.description: Approved local synthetic classification could be confused with complete acquisition, license, redistribution, or benchmark evidence.
risks.mitigation: Keep those data-card fields and benchmark-freeze/distribution gates explicitly limited; validator/minimal acceptance must never promote provenance or usage status.

risks.description: Stale strict-CARIN/negative-seed wording in task.json conflicts with the newly approved feature scope until the orchestrator reconciles it.
risks.mitigation: The orchestrator must update task-owned acceptance text before advancing state; contract/test workers must use the reconciled feature and architecture only after that source-of-truth alignment.

notes_for_next_agent: Orchestrator: reconcile task.json acceptance criteria with the approved compatibility boundary before advancing from PLANNING; workers must not edit task.json.

Contract work must replace strict-CARIN blocking semantics in packages.lock.json/boundary artifacts with the acceptance-versus-diagnostic model without changing the pinned evidence or suppressing findings.
The outcome schema must enforce canonical state ordering/exclusivity and the exact seed expectation: accepted plus minimal-profile-valid, carin-nonconformant, terminology-unverified.

Tester must independently cover every project rejection layer, CARIN evidence preservation/unavailability, opaque terminology, cross-file references, state combinations, sanitized findings, offline operation, and before/after dataset hashes.
Do not edit dataset/, infer code/extension meaning, dereference URLs, claim CARIN conformance, or add API/database/backend/frontend/infrastructure implementation in DATA-001.
PLATFORM-001 must preserve raw, compatibility decision, CARIN diagnostics, terminology uncertainty, normalized/derived artifacts, and human-authored decisions as distinct provenance classes.
